key_facts: The team is discussing cost-cutting measures for a remote control design.
There are currently 15 buttons, one LCD screen, one advanced chip-on-print, and a speech sensor in the design.
The special color of the buttons was initially included for a trendy look but is being reconsidered due to costs.
Kinetic energy is being replaced with a standard battery to reduce expenses.
Switching from a doubly curved to a single curved shape reduces production costs.
Dropping direct channel access buttons (1-9) in favor of using up/down arrows saves €4.50.
Using an integrated scroll-wheel push-button instead of multiple buttons could save money while maintaining functionality.
Speech recognition is expensive and difficult to implement reliably; it is proposed to be dropped.
The LCD screen remains essential despite its cost, as it provides key functionality and visual feedback.
Plastic is chosen over wood or rubber for the casing due to cost-effectiveness.
A total budget reduction of €3.50 is still needed after initial cuts.
Dropping the special color would save costs but might make the product less appealing.
An integrated scroll-wheel push-button is considered central to navigation and menu selection.
The design includes an infrared LED for proper functionality.
Team members express concerns about ease of use with the simplified interface.
Evaluation criteria include matching operating behavior, technological innovation, durability, and ease of use.
The team agrees on a score of approximately 3.1 for the overall product evaluation.
The final design involves a single curved, plastic remote with an LCD screen and one integrated scroll-wheel push-button.
The meeting concludes with plans to finalize reports and presentations before the deadline.
